title: Ethiopian Pancake (Serdo)
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Serdo — a thick, slightly sweet wheat pancake with cardamom and egg, cooked in a small amount of oil until golden. The Ethiopian street pancake — softer than Mulmul, cooked on both sides unlike injera, served with honey.
longDesc: Serdo fills the gap between injera (fermented, complex) and plain pancake (simple, neutral) — a slightly sweet, cardamom-fragrant thick pancake that is the street breakfast of Ethiopia's urban centres.
steps: Whisk flour, egg, sugar, cardamom, baking powder, and salt.
Add milk gradually — smooth, thick batter.
Heat pan. Add a little oil.
Pour ¼ cup batter. Cook 3—4 minutes until bubbles appear on surface.
chefTips: Thicker than a Western pancake — more like a drop scone.
Wait for bubbles on the surface before flipping.
cookingScience: The baking powder in Serdo (unlike Mulmul, which uses yeast) provides an immediate CO2 release when mixed with the liquid and acid in the batter — producing a less complex but faster rise than yeast fermentation.
culturalNote: Serdo is the everyday pancake of Ethiopian street breakfast — not as elaborate as injera, not as austere as Kita, it occupies the comfortable middle ground of Ethiopian morning food culture.
